subject.title: fix(exec-approvals): handle same-process sync/async lock contention

question: May synchronous exec-approval readers ever observe the pre-commit policy while a same-process async mutation holds the store lock, or must every authorization remain serialized with revocation and tightening?
rationale: The current patch trades availability for policy freshness at an execution authorization boundary, and choosing that contract requires explicit owner judgment rather than an automated workaround.

options.title: Preserve serialization
options.body: Replace the unlocked fallback with process-local coordination or an authoritative transaction snapshot and prove restrictive updates remain fail closed.

options.title: Accept stale reads
options.body: Land the fallback only if maintainers explicitly accept that a concurrent authorization can observe the previous complete policy snapshot.

options.title: Pause this patch
options.body: Keep the linked issue open while the mixed synchronous/asynchronous lock architecture is redesigned in owner-led work.

recommendation.title: Preserve serialization
recommendation.body: Replace the unlocked fallback with process-local coordination or an authoritative transaction snapshot and prove restrictive updates remain fail closed.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant merged hardening and serialization invariant appear to date to this person's recent exec-approval work.
